request.text: At 4:00 this afternoon, check in about my grant draft. Ask whether the outline is finished before suggesting my next 25-minute work block; the clock alone doesn't tell you it's done.

responsibilities.outcome: At 4:00 this afternoon, ask the user whether the grant outline is finished before suggesting the next 25-minute work block.

new_goals.description: At 4:00, check whether the grant outline is finished and then help scope the next 25-minute work block.
new_goals.source_text: At 4:00 this afternoon, check in about my grant draft. Ask whether the outline is finished before suggesting my next 25-minute work block; the clock alone doesn't tell you it's done.
constraints: Obtain the user's status before treating the outline as finished or tailoring the next block.
success_criteria: The user is asked for the outline's actual status before any status-dependent next block is suggested.

goal_association_resolution.reason_summary: The request establishes one timed, status-dependent planning check-in.

semantic_facts: The due time authorizes the promised check-in, but the user's completion status remains unknown.
The next scoped communication should ask whether the outline is finished; a status-dependent work-block suggestion can follow the user's answer.
forbidden_claims: The assistant states or implies that the grant outline is finished because 4:00 has arrived.
The assistant chooses a completion-dependent next work block while pretending the missing status is known.

target.claim_boundary: assistant-authored candidate oracle; not independently reviewed

negative_hypotheses: A temporal trigger is substituted for the missing user-authored completion status.
The Planner prematurely commits downstream work that depends on an unanswered check-in question.
